findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/triggers.py:107-126 (parse_hh_mm): `parts = at.split(":"); if len(parts) != 2: raise ValueError(f"{label} 'at' must be 'HH:MM', got {at!r}")`. Daily.__init__ (triggers.py:~407) calls parse_hh_mm(at, "Daily").
findings.explanation: run_daily only accepts "HH:MM". A "HH:MM:SS" string has three parts and raises ValueError.

findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:670-671 (schedule): `if not name: raise SchedulerNameRequiredError(...)`. Also scheduler.py:247-248 (add_job) and 565-566 (register). src/hassette/exceptions.py:704: `class SchedulerNameRequiredError(HassetteError)`, which derives from ReconstructibleError(Exception), not ValueError.
findings.explanation: An empty name raises SchedulerNameRequiredError. That class is not a ValueError subclass, so `except ValueError` would not catch it. Omitting `name` entirely does raise TypeError from the keyword-only parameter, so that half is correct.
findings.suggested_fix: Omitting it raises TypeError (no default value); an empty string raises SchedulerNameRequiredError.

findings.doc_quote: | jitter | float \| None | 0 | Random offset in seconds added to each run.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:596 (schedule) and every run_* method: `jitter: float | None = None,`
findings.explanation: The default for jitter is None, not 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Default column for jitter to `None`.

findings.doc_quote: Invoked on any exception, including CancelledError .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/core/command_executor.py:352-354: `except asyncio.CancelledError: enqueue_result_record(); raise`. The handler is spawned only after `_execute` returns normally (command_executor.py:540-552). scheduler.py:640-643 and classes.py:243 both say "excluding CancelledError".
findings.explanation: CancelledError is re-raised before the error-handler dispatch, so on_error is not invoked for it. It is invoked for other exceptions, including TimeoutError.
findings.suggested_fix: Invoked on any exception, including TimeoutError, but not CancelledError.

findings.doc_quote: triggered by hassette reload , or by config changes when automatic reloads are on
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/cli/__init__.py:74 `apps_app = App(name="app", ...)` and :114 `apps_app.command(cmd_app_reload, name="reload")`. There is no top-level `reload` command.
findings.explanation: The reload command is `hassette app reload`, not `hassette reload`.
findings.suggested_fix: triggered by `hassette app reload`, or by config changes when automatic reloads are on

findings.doc_quote: Each next run is calculated from wall-clock time, not from the previous run time.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/triggers.py:343-345 and 347-354: `next_run_time` returns `self.advance_past(previous_run, current_time)`, which advances the previous run's scheduled time by whole intervals.
findings.explanation: The next run is computed from the previous scheduled run time, snapped to the interval grid. It is not recomputed from the current wall-clock time. The grid is anchored at the first run, so execution delay does not cause drift. The sentence misdescribes the mechanism.
findings.suggested_fix: Each next run is the next tick on a fixed interval grid anchored at the first run, so slow handlers don't cause drift.

summary: Most of the page checks out: method signatures, defaults for run_in/run_every/run_minutely/run_hourly/run_once/register, if_exists semantics, the Job.matches field list, the if_past behavior for ZonedDateTime, the cron rules, and the global job_timeout_seconds. The errors are one wrong accepted format (HH:MM:SS for run_daily), one wrong exception class for an empty name, a wrong default for jitter, a wrong claim about on_error and CancelledError, a nonexistent CLI command, and a loose description of run_every's scheduling.
